group.passage:
Not long ago, most families bought new clothes only a few times a year, often when the seasons changed. Today, many popular brands [[1]] new styles every few weeks and sell them at prices so low that a T-shirt can cost less than a sandwich. This business model, known as fast fashion, has made clothing more affordable than ever, but it has also changed the way people value what they own.
When a shirt costs almost nothing, it begins to feel [[2]]: something to put on a few times and then throw away. Studies suggest that people now buy far more clothing than at the start of this century, yet keep each item for a much shorter time. A jacket that seemed fashionable in spring can look [[3]] by autumn. Shoppers who want to keep up with the [[4]] in fashion therefore feel pressure to buy again and again.
The low price tag hides a high cost for the planet. Growing cotton takes huge amounts of water, and the chemicals used to dye fabric often pollute rivers near factories. Clothes made of polyester and other synthetic materials also [[5]] tiny plastic fibers every time they are washed, and many of these end up in the ocean. Meanwhile, mountains of unwanted garments [[6]] in landfills around the world. Only a tiny [[7]] of old clothing is ever turned into new clothes; most of the rest is buried or burned. The human cost is just as serious. In 2013, a factory building in Bangladesh collapsed and killed more than a thousand garment workers, a tragedy that put the working conditions of the industry in the [[8]].
None of this means that people must stop shopping. Learning to [[9]] a torn shirt, buying secondhand, or swapping clothes with friends can all help. Choosing fewer but better-made clothes may cost more at first, but it is often the more [[10]] choice in the long run, for both the wallet and the planet.

1.explanation_zh: roll out 是「推出新產品」；roll 常用義是「滾動」，這裡是延伸義。第一句說過去一年只買幾次新衣，Today 形成對比：如今品牌每隔幾週就推出新款，並以極低的價格販售（and sell them）。
evidence: Not long ago, most families bought new clothes only a few times a year, often when the seasons changed.
Today, many popular brands [[1]] new styles every few weeks and sell them at prices so low that a T-shirt can cost less than a sandwich.

option_notes_zh.A: latest（形容詞（the latest 可作名詞），最新的；the latest 最新的東西）不合：空格是主詞 brands 的動詞，後接受詞 new styles，並與 sell 並列，需要及物動詞原形（現在式）。
option_notes_zh.B: disposable（形容詞，用完即丟的、拋棄式的）不合：空格是主詞 brands 的動詞，後接受詞 new styles，並與 sell 並列，需要及物動詞原形（現在式）。
option_notes_zh.C: spotlight 當動詞是「使受矚目」，但本句與第一句對比的是「多久推出一次新衣」，不是「讓哪些款式受注目」；spotlight 要放在第 8 格 in the spotlight。
option_notes_zh.D: economical（形容詞，經濟實惠的、節省的）不合：空格是主詞 brands 的動詞，後接受詞 new styles，並與 sell 並列，需要及物動詞原形（現在式）。
option_notes_zh.E: shed new styles 是「擺脫、丟掉新款式」，與後面 and sell them（並把它們拿來賣）矛盾。shed 屬於第 5 格。
option_notes_zh.F: share 當動詞是「分享」，brands share new styles 不能表示品牌推出商品來賣。
option_notes_zh.H: dated（形容詞，過時的、老派的）不合：空格是主詞 brands 的動詞，後接受詞 new styles，並與 sell 並列，需要及物動詞原形（現在式）。
option_notes_zh.I: mend new styles（修補新款式）不通。
option_notes_zh.J: pile up new styles 是「把新款式堆起來」，不是「推出」；every few weeks … and sell them 說的是定期上市販售。

translation_zh.text:
不久以前，大多數家庭一年只買幾次新衣服，通常是在換季的時候。如今，許多受歡迎的品牌每隔幾週就推出新款式，而且售價低到一件T恤比一個三明治還便宜。這種被稱為「快時尚」的商業模式讓衣服變得前所未有地平價，但也改變了人們看待自身所有物的方式。
當一件襯衫幾乎不花什麼錢時，它就開始讓人覺得是用完即丟的東西：穿個幾次就扔掉。研究指出，現在人們買的衣服比本世紀初多得多，但每件衣服留在身邊的時間卻短得多。一件春天看起來很時髦的外套，到了秋天可能就顯得過時。因此，想跟上最新流行的消費者會感到壓力，只好一買再買。
低廉的價格背後，是地球付出的高昂代價。種植棉花需要大量的水，用來染布的化學物質也常常污染工廠附近的河川。以聚酯纖維和其他合成材料製成的衣服，每次清洗時也會掉出細小的塑膠纖維，其中許多最後流入海洋。同時，堆積如山的廢棄衣物在世界各地的掩埋場裡越堆越高。舊衣物只有極小一部分會被做成新衣服，其餘大多被掩埋或焚燒。人所付出的代價也同樣嚴重。2013年，孟加拉一棟工廠大樓倒塌，造成一千多名成衣工人死亡，這場悲劇讓這個產業的勞動條件成為眾人關注的焦點。
這一切並不表示人們必須停止購物。學會縫補破掉的襯衫、購買二手衣，或和朋友交換衣服，都會有幫助。選擇數量較少但做工較好的衣服，一開始也許比較貴，但長期來看，無論對荷包還是對地球，往往都是比較划算的選擇。
